column1: # Reviewed source placement differences between the older Dreamcast build and
# the Windows/Mac shared source. Each row must identify a live source body and
# the exact Dreamcast file that still owns its matching written procedure.

column5: Complete selection destructor Windows583bb8..583c35 and Mac17b5b0..17b6bc contain virtual resource/CSprite dispose operations without calls to the ordinary namespace wrappers. Source retains canonical ResourceManager::dispose calls across TU; shared-header visibility is required to permit both compilers to expand wrappers. DC source owner is older snapshot evidence; preserve body/declaration, record exact reviewed Mac+Windows ownership divergence. This is not WIN_ONLY because DC counterpart exists.

The older Dreamcast line table attributes reset to Game.h. A shared inline header definition suppresses both claimed Windows functions in the integrated build.

Complete replaces the older DC fixed-array class (0x70d4 bytes) with a 0x7c-byte STL state. Mac constructor 0x98064 follows CampaignScenarioInfo::write and precedes its generated teardown/selectCampaign cluster; Mac xrefs identify TCampaignWindow, SavedGameHeader and game, whose Windows retail bodies retain constructor 0x489500. No cross-TU constructor expansion is observed. Moving the unchanged body to this source owner restores the retained call and all 11 named retail calls in SavedGameHeader (67.4607 to 100%). The declaration and all constructor uses remain shared.

Complete retains Windows 0x4897d0 and Mac 0x98448 in the campaign source cluster, and oldmain in kb.cpp retains a cross-TU call. Moving the unchanged vector scan from the header restores its 100% Windows body and the retained call; older DC has a header scan over its different fixed-array class. Declaration, fields and caller helper paths remain shared.

Complete Mac constructor 0xcf490 precedes reset/save/load and game::load. Twelve Mac sites identify game and selection callers; Windows retains eight selection-TU constructor calls but expands it inside game::load/save in the owning game TU. A source body before game::load preserves that visibility; the unchanged header body over-inlines it into GameSelectionHeadersStruct. Moving the canonical body restores all ten named calls and exact CFG/bytes there. Older DC Game.h:1301 remains snapshot evidence; fields and helper paths are unchanged.

Older DC retains a cache sweep in resourcemanager.cpp:2280. Complete Windows selection destructor 0x583b40 and Mac 0x17b504 have no cache-sweep operation or guard after the save-header teardown. Preserve the source call and canonical empty helper with shared-header visibility; the hidden source stub emitted a spurious Windows call. Exposing the same empty body restores all 34 Windows CFG blocks and 100% without flattening a helper.

column5: Older DC places the coordinate facade at drawing.cpp:666, dc 0x841d4. Complete Windows army::rangeAttack 0x43f900 expands its fixed-viewport delegation across translation units; shared-header visibility removes the extra facade call and raises the comparison 94.47 to 99.50 while retaining the canonical SLimitData overload. Mac rangeAttack 0x4b62c likewise contains no coordinate-facade call; retained drawing bodies at 0xa4e6c (resetLimitCreature), 0xa4ef0 (updateCombatArea), and 0xa4f6c (following effect routine) provide no separate facade at the older source-order slot. This is a reviewed Complete source-placement inference, not recovered DC header ownership or proof of an original inline keyword.
